The Vaal and Raw Sewerage

By: Anna-Maria van Niekerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Raw sewerage destined for the Vaal?

Summary:
Supposed plans for Township sewage to be piped into Vaal Dam at Deneysville. Source of drinking water at risk from non-functional council. Bad enough that Vaal is contaminated by farms etc upstream of the dam but now raw sewerage. An email was sent from DWS stating that the construction is now halted until Metsimaholo Local Municipality applies for authorisation.

Further information:
Destruction of the Vaal Dam. The Vaal Dam has a catchment area covering 38 505 square kilometres and a capacity to hold 2575 million cubic metres of water which, under normal circumstances and without a substantial inflow, will last for 2 years. This dam has a surface area of 321 square kilometres and an average depth of 22,5 metres. The above catchment area is home to thousands of birds (the Fish Eagle recently come home), Duiker, Many cats, Jackals, insects, The famous bull frog and many thousands of others species. R9,7 million has been allocated for a so called sanitation project The raw sewage pipe is for a massive settlement called Refengkhotso This sewerage waste will be pumped directly into the Vaal Dam causing major contamination to humans and all wildlife in this massive area of water. The existing sewers built in 2012 no longer work due to lack of maintenance and misuse of Municipal and government funds...no surprise there.. Firstly is does not cost 9.7 million rand to run a +-15 km raw sewage pipeline and secondly it would not cost near to this amount to fix the existing sewers. This project smells of another excuse to back-pocket money that belongs to the tax payer. It seems that this project is based on corruption and greed..SIMPLE The Negative impact on the environment of dumping raw sewage into the Vaal are as follows: Depending on its content and level of treatment, sewage can wreak havoc all the way up the food chain to humans. Raw, untreated sewage, for example, may contain harmful chemicals, hazardous compounds, heavy metals, and viruses. ance and the misuse of Government funds. All signed petitions in the area have been ignored by the powers that be. Please help us to prevent the sewerage pipeline from from reaching completion

Press Release:


PROMOS:

Fifteen second

VO: The Vaal Dam – a critical water source to millions of people and industries…but rising pollution from defunct sewerage works on its shores seriously threaten its future.


Fifteen second

DR SHAN HOLMES, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST: We’re pumping pristine water from the Lesotho Scheme as it makes its way into the Vaal into what is becoming a concentrated cesspool.

VO: Vaal dam water under serious threat from sewage contamination. Who’s to blame?


Ten second

VO: Sewage spilling into the streets, sewage diverted past a key pump station… Deneysville’s wastewater treatment plant is 90% over capacity, threatening contamination of the nearby Vaal Dam.

Script:


DENEYSVILLE SEWAGE


STORY SCRIPT:
The Lesotho Highlands Water Project was built at a cost of over R16-billion to ensure water-stressed South Africa’s survival. The South African government is currently looking for R10-billion for a third big dam there.
The pristine water is the lifeblood of 45% of South Africa’s people and 60% of its industry.
This is where it lands up – the Vaal Dam that stretches across Gauteng and the Free State.
And this is what becomes of it.
Regular water quality tests done by Rand Water as they extract and purify the water to drinking standard, show rising and unacceptable e-coli counts. Environmental scientist Dr Shan Holmes has watched the numbers rise for years.
DR SHAN HOLMES, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST: We’re pumping pristine water on many levels from the Lesotho Scheme as it makes its way into the Vaal into what is becoming a concentrated cesspool of industrial, mining pollution and now a massive organic load. You’re looking at a potential of cholera, typhus, salmonella outbreaks. This has an immediate and is a major risk for public health.
Manten Marina is a family business that’s relied on the Vaal Dam for its livelihood since 1975. Kathy Manten grew up in the business.
KATHY MANTEN: The water quality, you used to be able to drink it, literally, with a scoopful out of the dam while you were sailing and it was quite safe to do to so.
For at least five years now Kathy has watched correspondence pile up between residents of Deneysville alongside the Vaal and the manager of the Metsimaholo municipality, about the poor quality of water entering the Dam from towns on the shores.
KATHY MANTEN: And it’s our drinking water for the rest of the country – or for Gauteng at least and if it’s polluted it’s such a huge body of water – to try and correct that will be a nightmare.
A stone’s throw away is the township Refengkgotso. Paulina Meketsi has worked hard at her job in Johannesburg to set up her family home here near the Vaal Dam. Brutal stench permeates the air around her home.
PAULINA MEKETSI: We can’t go anywhere else, this is home.
Paulina’s asthma is triggered every time she confronts the thick air from pools of raw sewage spewing from defunct inspection holes in the pipeline at the back of her home.
Local businessman turned DA councillor Johannes Mofokeng is trying to resolve issues from the inside – but to no avail.
JOHANNES MOFOKENG, DA Councillor: The cattles (sic) of the people are living in here, drinking the very same water and when it’s weddings or funerals, they’re slaughtering the very same cattle. .
Word travelled fast as Carte Blanche arrived at the Deneysville sewage treatment plant. We were swamped by local activists, residents and opposition politicians. Irene Main watches the dam on behalf of the NGO SAVE.
IRENE MAIN, SAVE THE VAAL ENVIRONMENT: I would say first of all, they’ve allowed development to take place without upgrading the necessary infrastructure…
DEREK WATTS: Why hasn’t it been upgraded?
IRENE MAIN: At the Forum meeting that we had on Thursday last week they said they don’t have the funds…
DA councillor Dr Albe Viljoen blames aging infrastructure.
DEREK WATTS: Initially, how many houses, how many people was this treatment plant meant to cater for?
ALBE VILJOEN: This is bio-filters and that’s only good for communities for 2 or 3, maybe 4000 people if all the sewage comes here – so that’s why the thing is over-capacitated. There’s about now 20 000 just in the townships.
DEREK WATTS: While we’ve been talking here more people have arrived…and it’s obviously a very big issue in the area.
ANDRE JOHNSON: There’s a pump station over there with only one auger working…for months. There was a time that no auger was working. You can go there…Friday they were still fighting blockage (sic) drains.
Retired mine surveyor Peet Schabort has been keeping a photo record of the faulty system – sewage flooding the cemetery and on into the Vaal Dam. About a year ago, deep trenches were dug to capture the sewage flowing from the township, diverted past broken pumps.
ANDRE JOHNSON: Up here is a pump station over there, we will show you – if you go after 4pm they will have disconnected the pipe, and then they pump the sewage into the veld.
DEREK WATTS: Just into the bush, hey?
ANDRE JOHNSON: And you can drive along there, you can’t open the window, you die.
DEREK LINK: This treatment plant – clearly unable to deal with the amount of sewage it’s meant to process is just half the problem – a disturbing and unhealthy amount of sewage isn’t even reaching this plant.
Outrage over the overworked treatment system flared into a full-scale local war a few months ago, when residents discovered that their municipality that had set aside R9,7-million for upgrading the treatment plant, was instead building a new pipe to take treated effluent from the treatment works to the Dam.
PEET SCHABORT: It’s those pipes next to that little white and blue building.
DEREK WATTS: Yes, I see.
ANDRE JOHNSON: And it’s been dug – no one was consulted, no-one was informed, nothing.
PEET SCHABORT: And another thing with this pipeline – as quickly as they lay it, they covered it. In other words, the stones that were dug up were piled on top and in time they will push through the pipe.
Vice chairman of the Deneysville Residents’ committee Bill Eardly walked door to door to petition for signatures against the pipeline.
BILL EARDLY: It’s discharging into a part of the dam where there is no current, no winds and it’s just going to be a septic tank on the side of the dam.
National Department of Water and Sanitation spokesman, Sputnik Ratau said when they discovered the matter of the pipeline, and especially as it was initially constructed to run through a sensitive wetland, swift action followed.
SPUTNIK RATAU: For any water use, as a water use authority, you need to have authorisation as per the dictates of the National Water Act. For as long as we do not have an application that says we would like to do this…that’s why we asked them to stop the work that they were doing because they didn’t have the necessary authorisation.
All fingers on the new pipeline and the over-capacity treatment works point to Metsimaholo Municipality. Spokesman Gino Alberts admits they’d continued without authorisation.
DEREK WATTS: The national department says you didn’t make an application.
DR GINO ALBERTS: We didn’t get an authorisation –
DEREK WATTS: Why not?
DR GINO ALBERTS: it was an oversight from our side. We thought that the operating licence that we have is sufficient.
DEREK LINK: This is the outlet from the original pipeline into the Vaal Dam – as you can see it’s only a few hundred metres from where water is abstracted as they call it, supplying roughly 12-million people.
It is from this pipeline that residents complain insufficiently treated effluent is polluting their dam – in addition to the sewage that seeps straight into ground water and runs over the surface into the Vaal.
IRENE MAIN: In untreated sewage you get two pests – one is cryptosporidium and the other is giardia. In a meeting a year ago Rand Water actually advised us they were picking up these two pests in their filtration process…while they can treat this, it’s expensive to treat it. And at the end of the day the cost is going to be passed on to the consumer.
Backing up the charge of pollution is yet another in a series of Quarterly Water Quality Status reports of the Vaal Dam Reservoir released by Rand Water. For Deneysville – and most other towns around the Vaal, e-coli and salt counts are listed as “unacceptable”.
DEREK WATTS: But it looks like raw sewage is finding its way directly into the Vaal…
GINO ALBERTS: Those are claims…allegations. But what I want to state – I want to state it very categorical. We are a very caring and responsible government that won’t expose our people to health hazardous conditions.
DEREK: The real problem is it’s a violation of human rights.
DR GINO ALBERTS: I totally disagree totally with that, because we are, like I said, are taking our people’s life very seriously and we are ensuring that we address all the issues with regard to the sewage plant. Like I’ve indicated, the raw sewer at the pump station is because of vandalism that we have admitted as a municipality we have to beef up the security.
DEREK WATTS: Will moving this discharge point make a difference?
DR GINO ALBERTS: We believe so – that is why we have started with the project because it will assist us a lot, because remember the current one is position is not where we want it to be – it’s next to the road and we are looking as a municipality, because of the growth of the town, we want to make development next to the road and where the pipe is currently – that is why we want to change the position.
KATHY MANTEN: They’re planning on bringing another 2500 people into the area and there’s no infrastructure to support them. There’s nothing for these people. There’s not even industry here.
Peet’s photographs and the Deneysville pipeline have galvanised support from the conservation community.

SHAN HOLMES: These practices are in fact a clear-cut case of water pollution that is in fact criminally libellous. This is a time-bomb with a not so long fuse…where we are going to deliberately and knowingly shoot up the costs of water and impact on our water availability.

It is from this pipeline that residents complain insufficiently treated effluent is polluting their dam – in addition to the sewage that seeps straight into ground water and runs over the surface into the Vaal. IRENE MAIN: In untreated sewage you get two pests – one is cryptosporidium and the other is giardia. In a meeting a year ago Rand Water actually advised us they were picking up these two pests in their filtration process…while they can treat this, it’s expensive to treat it. And at the end of the day the cost is going to be passed on to the consumer. Backing up the charge of pollution is yet another in a series of Quarterly Water Quality Status reports of the Vaal Dam Reservoir released by Rand Water. For Deneysville – and most other towns around the Vaal, e-coli and salt counts are listed as “unacceptable”. DEREK WATTS: But it looks like raw sewage is finding its way directly into the Vaal… GINO ALBERTS: Those are claims…allegations. But what I want to state – I want to state it very categorical. We are a very caring and responsible government that won’t expose our people to health hazardous conditions. DEREK: The real problem is it’s a violation of human rights. DR GINO ALBERTS: I totally disagree totally with that, because we are, like I said, are taking our people’s life very seriously and we are ensuring that we address all the issues with regard to the sewage plant. Like I’ve indicated, the raw sewer at the pump station is because of vandalism that we have admitted as a municipality we have to beef up the security. DEREK WATTS: Will moving this discharge point make a difference? DR GINO ALBERTS: We believe so – that is why we have started with the project because it will assist us a lot, because remember the current one is position is not where we want it to be – it’s next to the road and we are looking as a municipality, because of the growth of the town, we want to make development next to the road and where the pipe is currently – that is why we want to change the position. KATHY MANTEN: They’re planning on bringing another 2500 people into the area and there’s no infrastructure to support them. There’s nothing for these people. There’s not even industry here. Peet’s photographs and the Deneysville pipeline have galvanised support from the conservation community. SHAN HOLMES: These practices are in fact a clear-cut case of water pollution that is in fact criminally libellous. This is a time-bomb with a not so long fuse…where we are going to deliberately and knowingly shoot up the costs of water and impact on our water availability.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Raw sewerage destined for the Vaal?
metadata.Summary: Supposed plans for Township sewage to be piped into Vaal Dam at Deneysville. Source of drinking water at risk from non-functional council. Bad enough that Vaal is contaminated by farms etc upstream of the dam but now raw sewerage. An email was sent from DWS stating that the construction is now halted until Metsimaholo Local Municipality applies for authorisation.
metadata.Further information: Destruction of the Vaal Dam. The Vaal Dam has a catchment area covering 38 505 square kilometres and a capacity to hold 2575 million cubic metres of water which, under normal circumstances and without a substantial inflow, will last for 2 years. This dam has a surface area of 321 square kilometres and an average depth of 22,5 metres. The above catchment area is home to thousands of birds (the Fish Eagle recently come home), Duiker, Many cats, Jackals, insects, The famous bull frog and many thousands of others species. R9,7 million has been allocated for a so called sanitation project The raw sewage pipe is for a massive settlement called Refengkhotso This sewerage waste will be pumped directly into the Vaal Dam causing major contamination to humans and all wildlife in this massive area of water. The existing sewers built in 2012 no longer work due to lack of maintenance and misuse of Municipal and government funds...no surprise there.. Firstly is does not cost 9.7 million rand to run a +-15 km raw sewage pipeline and secondly it would not cost near to this amount to fix the existing sewers. This project smells of another excuse to back-pocket money that belongs to the tax payer. It seems that this project is based on corruption and greed..SIMPLE The Negative impact on the environment of dumping raw sewage into the Vaal are as follows: Depending on its content and level of treatment, sewage can wreak havoc all the way up the food chain to humans. Raw, untreated sewage, for example, may contain harmful chemicals, hazardous compounds, heavy metals, and viruses. ance and the misuse of Government funds. All signed petitions in the area have been ignored by the powers that be. Please help us to prevent the sewerage pipeline from from reaching completion
